newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schiphol to unveil underground cargo options - Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: Schiphol to unveil underground cargo options - Feb 4.

text.p: Details of a feasibility study looking at an innovative underground cargo transport system will be unveiled at a press conference February 4.

Frits Bisschop, director of cargo at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport told Reuters in an interview so-called Underground Logistic System (ULS) could have considerable scope to transfer airfreight between Schiphol and any new national airport the Dutch government might built.
The airport has been been carefully looking at the size of the transport tube, the size of pallets, detailing the cost benefit analysis and is more or less choosing where to go next.
"I don't want to give too much away, but I am very optimistic about the prospects for this project," said Bisschop.
The pros and cons of a second national airport will be the focus of a major debate between Dutch MPs starting in February.
"Whatever option we choose we will have to ensure that cargo can access whatever new national airport is built," Bisschop said.
"I feel the ULS we have been studying may provide some long term answers about how cargo can access any new airport that may (or may not) be built in the Netherlands."

The ULS has been proposed as a possible means of quickly moving freight to and from the airport to a rail centre at nearby Hoofdorp or a major customer base, the Dutch flower auction at the town of Aalsmeer.
"If you can move freight in this triangle then you can move it to whatever location you choose," said Bisschop: .
He said he would welcome a new airport which could have 24 hour freight operations, and that the possibilities for new business are "endless."

The airport operating company last year launched a study looking at three potential new airport options. One was to build an island at an unspecified location in the North Sea; another to reclaim land from the inner reaches of the IJsselmeer, a large, man-made expanse of water near Amsterdam; and a third would be an airport at the mouth of the port of Rotterdam, on a proposed land reclamation site called the Tweede Maasvlakte. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
